review_text: 1. Buy or Do Not Buy?,Buy It.,2. What is so good about this?,It is a unique toy, so much fun. It’s a mini helicopter/drone, but packs quite a punch. It is affordable, and so worth the entertainment you receive in return. The basic idea is it floats up in the air like a helicopter, and comes down. Your job is to position an object or your hand under the toy as it drops to trigger it to fly straight back up again, the longer your hand/object is placed under the toy, the higher the toy will rise. The toy lights up beautifully, which makes playing in the dark super fun, inside or outside.,3. How do you play with it?,Don’t make the mistake I made, and not read the instructions. Actually, I still haven’t read it 😊, and figure out how to play with it correctly by purely by accident, albeit after several knocks and falls…of the toy, not me. Turn on the toy by pressing the black rubber button at the bottom of the toy. Hold the toy on your hand upright, press the button on the remote to turn on the blades, then let it go. No need to push it up…just let it go. As it floats up and comes down, just place your hand under the toy to make it rise again.,To avoid potentially damaging the toy, know that there is a sensor under the body (ball) of the toy. The longer your hand or any object is under the sensor, the higher the toy will rise. So, when you get started playing with the toy, and wonder like I did, why it keeps going up and being stuck on the ceiling, you are probably placing your hand under the sensor for too long. No worries, if you are too short to grab the toy as it floats under the ceiling, just press the button again, and after a couple of seconds, you will notice the blades slow down and the toy drop, just press the button again to make it rise again to avoid hitting the floor.,4. How much of playtime do you get with it?,About 10 minutes. I charge it for about 20 minutes, and have been getting about 10 minutes of continuous play time. Given the size of the toy, I think this is probably as long as the charge can hold.,5. Is it safe?,I think so. The blades are plastic, and flexible. They are not hard. As long as you play it the right away, you should not hurt yourself. Also, the fact that it floats up means that it will rise anytime something is under it, so the chances of it hitting your eyes or injuring you otherwise is small as long as you are not throwing it horizontally. The ball/base is clear plastic. It is not heavy or metal-like, so no danger there. Small kids should play under adult supervision.

I have not tried painting yet, but the air stream on my hand was tight when held close and broadened as I took it slowly away. The key to making any airbrush work properly is good cleaning habits and paint/thinner mixture. I will post my results on the airbrush later.,My overall finding is this is going to be a great addition to my model making tools. Once you are through the setup process, you can switch back to your home 5 GHz network. This is noted in the Quick Start guide but it is easy to miss. The sharp color screen of the digital weather station will illuminate continuously with a USB charging cable during power operation, and when charging by USB, there are 4 different models of brightness. To save energy from batteries, the LCD color display would not light up automatically in battery mode. You can touch the top of the weather station, then it will become evoked.,The ability to remotely view weather conditions at one's home and the NWS forecast are nice features. Certainly not for the true meteorology aficionado but more than enough for a quick and dirty view of the weather.

review_text: I have been a trainer for many years and always felt "shock" collars weren't the humane way to train until our new dog just wouldn't stop barking for no reason. I tried the vibrate and the "shock" mode on myself before I put it on her. 1st, Vibrate mode is a soft shake of the device. My kids and I had fun passing it around to try each level. 2nd, "Shock" mode isn't the type of shock these devices used to have. It's static shock, like dragging your feet across the floor and then touching someone hoping there's a shock for fun. Level 100 isn't fun. Just FYI. And no I did not let my kids try shock mode.  It can work automatically (Auto Anti-Bark Mode) without manual remote control, and it can also be switched to "Remote Control Mode" to train your dog manually. (The receiver collar will enter "Auto Anti-Bark Mode" automatically if you don’t use the remote control in the first 1 minute after turning on the collar. So please press any button on the remote if you want to enter "Remote Control Mode" ),In one day our dog stopped ALL bad behavior. I only used the shock mode once. I start with asking her to stop barking and use the beep mode. She didn't listen so I used the vibrate level 50. She was confused and continued to bark a little. I gave her the enough command to stop and gave her the shock mode level 50. She immediately laid down and stopped. I've never used shock mode since. She is very smart and learned the beep means business. I'd say 90% of the time she listens with the beep and the other 10% is just vibrate on level 25. I ONLY wanted it for problem barking but she is an absolute angel in all ways. She doesn't even beg for food anymore or ambush family when they walk in. She's calmed down and is also more gentle with my kids. She's still the happy, goofy, 90 pound Bernese Mountain Dog she always was but with manners. It's only been 3 days and everyone is very pleased with the results. I love that the seller contacted us twice to make sure all was well. It was easy to set up and use as well. I couldn't be happier to be able to have conversations with folks outside and not have her barking like a psychopath. My dog is the good dog on the block now.

So, I needed a replacement soon, especially with so much of the time being spent indoors nowadays because of COVID.,I had pretty much given up on indoor antennas, and was looking for an outdoor antenna because generally you get more channels and the signal is stable with outdoor antennas, however they are pricey and the thought of getting on my roof to install it dissuaded it, so I decided to look for an indoor antenna and landed upon this.,What’s good?,1. Easy installation - Installation is a breeze. I like the fact that it comes with an option to install the base in the bottom or on the side/back (see pictures). You get screws if you want to affix it to the wall. Please note that although it does come with a USB charger, it does not come with a USB plug, but you can use any standard plug to hook up the cord to. The antenna will light up blue at the bottom if it’s receiving power.,2. More channels – I tested both my old antenna (brand name withheld) and this antenna. With my old antenna, I received 21 channels. With this antenna, I received 33 channels (see pictures). So an addition of 10. Kidding, just making sure you were paying attention 😊. Actually, an addition of 12. I placed both antennas in the same position for this test and I just ran standard auto-program on my TV to get the results. My area is supposed to get up to 47 channels based on channelmaster.com, but many of the channels have weak signal strength in my area, so 33 is pretty good. But I got the main channels I needed, so no complaints. Don’t feel like I am missing anything important. Note: I also tested this on my other TV that’s closer to the window, and was able to get 41 channels.,3. Signal strength and stability - After several hours continuous watching, I can see a noticeable difference between this and my old antenna. Not only do I get more channels, but the signal is stable. It does not break when there are disruptions like people movement near the antenna/TV.,Overall, I am satisfied with this antenna, and is such an upgrade over my old one. review_title: Super fast ssd! From a great company! You won't regret getting one of these!
review_text: So first off this drive is a bit on the expensive side. But totally worth it, it's one of the fastest external drives I've used. Mine totaled 953gb.it has decent locking software included on the drive. But I don’t tend to need these. My testing computer is a 2016 gaming computer, with its aging components this Ravpower drive was still super fast. My internal main drive is a SanDisk ultra 2 240gb SSD (550mbps read and 500mbps Wright). My secondary hdd is a standard 2.5in 1TB Western Digital Scorpio SATA laptop drive. 24gb of 1600mhz ram. I did many copies to and from each drive while some used my system ram to “ boost “ performance a bit. I also cleared this for a fresh copy to see the difference. Some of these actually hit the theoretical limit of my system. A newer system may see slightly higher numbers, or a internal benchmark may also see different numbers, I went for actual file transfers, Make sure to check my screenshots. They show multiple transfers. I noticed many other pictures in reviews showing benchmarks so I stayed with actual transfers. I figured it would be pointless to just show more of the same. This drive is just fast. But remember it's only as fast as your computers slowest part. In my case it's my cpu lanes. I have a few 3.0 ports, but there from a generation ago, I don’t have any 3.1 ports or any type C or thunderbolt ports to test on. But I still commonly hit 200-400mbps, and I believe some of these numbers were because the buffer in my internal drive ran out, but from the ram buffer it hit over 1gbps (see pictures). I also did smaller file transfers. Which also went surprisingly fast, I also compared this to my PNY 128gb 3.0 usb the Ravpower nearly doubled the PNY in each of the file transfers. I’ll post some number with what hdd I went to and from.  I’ll attach pictures of most of these test, some of them go quite fast., Next are technical tests, if your not interested please skip to the bottom.,-------------------------,From Ravpower ssd to internal ssd- 6.45gb single file ( windows 10 install iso file ) took approx 4-6 seconds, approx speed was 1.42gbps (see picuter).,Next was internal ssd to external Ravpower ssd- same 6.45gb file as before, took approx 12 seconds, it started at just over 1.2gbps and at 42% tapered off to 476mbps.,Next was from the internal WesternDigital hdd, to the Ravpower external ssd. It was a combination of the windows 10 file from before and several hundred pictures. This one started at 60mbps then went up to 104 and ran at this speed for the last 13gb. ( 13.5gb total ) took about 2 minutes.,Next was the same file as previous copy, but now it was the Ravpower ssd to the internal Sandisk ssd. It ran at 386 mbps for the entire 13.5gb, took about 30-35 seconds.,Next was the same file again, and went from Ravpower ssd to the Sandisk ssd (second time), this ran 400mbps for 50% of the transfer then dropped to 165mbps for the remainder of the transfer, this took just under 30 seconds.,Next I re-ran the previous 13.5gb file from the SanDisk ssd to Ravpower ssd, it slow for about 4 seconds, it started around 20mbps but quickly ramped up to 240mbps by 10% and ran at this speed for the remainder of the transfer. It took about 35 seconds total.,Next was a folder with approx 24,000 files. 85% were music files most other’s were properties folders and sub folders. It was being transferred from the internal WesternDigial hdd to the Ravpower ssd. It was just under 99gb. It started right at 125mbps, with an estimated 15 minute transfer time. For this transfer windows showed the hdd was running at 82% for the entire transfer. It ran at 125mbps until 82% then the average dropped to 90mbps for the remaining 14gb. The total transfer time was around what it estimated.,Next was the same file of music from the WesternDigital hdd back to the Ravpower ssd. It started at 120mbps, but within 1% held at 30mbps for the rest of the transfer. Which took around a half an hour. Now I believe this was a bottleneck of the internal hdd, as it was at 100% usage the entire time. This was a standard laptop hard drive, most people with entry level computers should expect simular results as this. **Now that being said, moving 99gb in about 30-40 minutes is still amazingly fast. My 3.0 pny 128gb flash drive took nearly 3 times longer for this same transfer. **,Next was a copy of approx 5,000 songs. I had to keep it under 25gb to avoid filling the Sandisk ssd, so I copied 19gb of music. I started by copying 19gb from the Ravpower ssd to the internal Sandisk ssd. It ran at 238mbps for about 10% then averaged 124mbps for the rest, it took about 50 to 90 seconds to copy the 19gb which was around 7,000 files 5,000 of which were music files. The rest were properties files and sub folders.,The last transfer will be from the Sandisk internal ssd to the Ravpower external ssd. It will the the same 19gb as the previous test. This averaged around 170mbps and took about 100 seconds.,I left my system resource monitor running in the background you can see in most pictures so you can see the computer's status while copying., --------------------------,In closing, this hard drive is amazingly fast for its size and price. Has a great storage capacity for its size and was very stable while using. I never had any problems copying or moving files as I have with some others ive tested. It holds a stable speed for most of the transfers so you have a close idea of the finish time. Others ive tested jump around so much you have no clue how long it will actually take. These were all real world tests with actual files, I didn’t use any benchmarks to get my numbers. As shown in the pictures I went solely off of the windows 10 status bar. Most of the time my internal hdd was maxed out while writing or reading to or from the external ssd, which I expected as its rated much faster. Many times it maxed out my internal ssd as well showing its clearly faster then them most of the time. This drive will work for the majority of people even tech savvy people working on computers.

Make sure all items/components are tight, secure, & dry!,The programming was prob the most difficult, but its so worth it for the benefits! Now it find it fairly easy! It would be nice if the screen had a blue back light or something so it's easier to see. Think grey screen with black letters; that's what this display is like. When programmed and ready, it shows the buttons are locked and the next time for feeding!,I've heard some say they had issues.,I did buy the adapter separately. I've since had 2 power outages and all I have to do is set the time and then set to custom (vs the preprogrammed cat or dog) and it remembers the feeding schedule without me having to reschedule the feedings! Very thankful for that lil feature since power outages are very common in the summer here!,You will have to force feedings a couple times because the conveyor doesnt have food on it! At first I was like wth! But after doing a couple force feedings, it worked perfectly.,TIP: dont use slow feed unless you have larger portions. Since you can schedule up to 12 feedings with 1/8c as your lowest, I just do multiple 1/4c feedings. The smaller amounts just take way too long to dispense on slow feed!,We use blue buffalo cat kibbles and have no issues with jamming.,It took about 2 months for my cats to correlate the feeder with feeding rather than us making it magically happen. review_title: Very quiet hair dryer, albeit a little less in wattage
review_text: This is nice 1600-watt hair dryer. It is pretty lightweight for its size and oddly attractive. More importantly, it is significantly quieter than most hair dryers that I have tried or heard. I really appreciate that I no longer have to hold a high-noise hair dry close to my ears for 5-10 minutes and there is no more high-pitched whining sound to tolerate. However, it is a little low in wattage but good enough for my short hairs. If you have long, thick hair, you may find it a little lacking in power though.,The cord is not retractable but plenty long enough for me (6+ feet long). There are three controls on the handle - two rocker switches for high/low speed and high/low heat respectively, and one push button for a blast of cold air. You need to hold the push button for the cold air to blow though. The rocker switches are easy to select and give you the visual of the particular settings they are in. A detachable concentrator nozzle is provided. A hang loop is integrated into the bottom of the handle, which is handy.,The hair dryer could have use some improvement in ergonomics. I don't find it very comfortable to hold for long duration due to the shape of the handle. It is not terrible but just okay for me. I have had hair dryers that are more much comfortable to hold and grip.,All in all, this is a good hair dryer. It isn't the most powerful but it is very quiet. If you value low noise over power, this is the dryer for you. If you have long, thick hair that doesn't dry as fast, you may be happier with a higher wattage dryer.

review_title: Great traps but only humane with responsible use
review_text: Caution-  Put your trap where you can get to it easily, and check it frequently depending upon the weather in your area. These tiny creatures  dehydrate very quickly and easily even in cold weather. Because they are small they will overheat or freeze to death very quickly. Rodents are nocturnal,  when you catch them it will probably be at night so be certain to check your traps as early as you possibly can in the morning.  If your schedule does not allow for safe checking times, simply don’t put them out until you have time. Please, don’t ask me how I know, sadly, from a horrifying experience. They are only as humane as you make them. With that said, these are great traps. However, maybe I didn’t thoroughly read the description but they are smaller than I  expected.  I think they should be twice the size of what they are.  Also, if you truly want to be humane, have your “exit“ strategy preplanned. Be certain to let them go in an area that has fresh, available water and quick cover. Try to release them in the morning so that they have time to find a safe place before the nocturnal hunters come out.

review_title: Great sound machine for sleeping and relaxation
review_text: I'm pleasantly surprised with this little sound machine. It is great for sleeping and relaxation when a little bit of ambient sound is desirable. It's the size of a alarm clock and lightweight, and quite portable.,The machine has a nice range of natural sounds, fan noise and white noise, such as the sound of waterfalls, ocean waves, rainforest, birds, different types of fans, etc. The quality of the sound is okay. Just don't expect a high fidelity sound. The sound comes from both sides of the machine, so it would work equally well on either side of the bed. One thing though. This machine can get pretty loud. Quite handy if you need it to drown some loud background noise.,On the top of the machine are push button controls - power, volume up and down, fan noise, white noise and natural sounds, loop and timer. The 3 sound buttons cycle through various kinds of sound in their own category. I appreciate that a timer is available for 30, 60 and 90 minutes (3 LED lights to confirm your selection), so I don't have to run the sound throughout the night.,The machine runs on either USB power (5VDC @ 0.5-3A)  or 4 AA batteries. Only a micro-USB cable is provided (along with a user manual). You'll have to provide your own USB power adapter or the batteries. There is a pass-through USB port at the back of the machine, which is handy if you want to charge your phone while the machine is plugged in.,All in all, this is a nice little sound machine for sleeping and relaxation. After trying it out, I have to admit that it works well for its intended purposes. I found it works best at lower volumes, just a bit louder than the ambient noise level. When it gets too loud, it starts to lose sound fidelity and become annoying (especially for certain sounds such as waves and heartbeat).

review_text: This is a pretty good set of wireless headphones with a charging case. They are very simple to set up and use. The headphones are held in their case with magnets, so you just pop them in and they turn themselves off and start charging. The case has a battery and can charge the headphones without being plugged in.,The headphones each have a touch sensitive button on the side. Touching the right ear turns the volume up, and the left ear turns the volume. Double taps act like play/pause and triple taps skip tracks. Its a very intuitive interface and fairly responsive. Sometimes there is a delay, but most of the time the earphones respond as expected.,The sound is good for the price. Don’t expect deep bass tones or crisp highs, but you do get a decent sound, reliable wireless connectivity, and an easy to use interface.

review_text: I've had the G20 for about 3 months and use them daily (primarily for music and media). I also have a half-dozen sets of other earbuds taking up drawer space because either the sound quality or feature set disappointed. I've become a fan of ENACFIRE and bought the G20 to upgrade from my ENACFIRE Future Plus earbuds because of sound and feature improvements. The G20 have a low profile and fit snugly, but comfortably, in my ears. The sound is clear, slightly bass-heavy, with great stereo separation. I occasionally use the earbuds for phone calls and they work/sound fine. The ear tips provide good sound isolation (the noise cancellation feature is for phone calls only). The Smart Touch Control features set the G20 apart from competitors at a similar price point. Very light sequences of long and short touches activate/deactivate the earbuds, connect to your phone's smart assistant, raise/lower the volume, pause/forward/reverse your track selection, etc. Other earbuds at this price point (including the Future Plus I previously purchased) have mechanical buttons that are painful to your ear canal because they require quite a bit of pressure to depress. The G20 earbuds pair quickly and have voice feedback to let you know when the earbuds are powering up/down and pairing/connected. The earbuds work as a pair or individually, though some features are only present in one earbud (e.g. the volume up and down functions are split between the right and left earbud). The advertised battery life is accurate and the storage case doubles as a charger.

review_text: Over the years, I've learned to trust my instincts (and legit --not bot/fake-- reviews on Amazon) when it comes to audio devices, because with my researched purchases, I really haven't needed to default to big, expensive brand names. And, in fact, some lesser-known, or even unknown Chinese brands have had AS GOOD or BETTER sound and build quality as the big brands.  These bluetooth ear buds are no exception.  I haven't tested the battery life claims yet, but I have a feeling, on my long, 13-hour transatlantic flights, I'll need to have my wired sport ear buds handy for continuous use. However, the noise cancellation of these bluetooth ear buds, and still-stellar battery life, will be worth testing on my next trip.,For the best bass, clarity, and depth of sound, be sure you're using the correct size of ear bud inserts. The "average" size comes already attached to the ear buds, and the smaller size is included in a small bag in the packaging. Also, be sure your phone's music player EQ is optimized for the in-ear experience. The fit is only between two sizes, and not three like a lot of other in-ear products I've used over the years, but the standard size works pretty well for me. It takes some getting used to having ear buds in my ears, and until you do get used to that, you may have pretty sore ears for awhile. I think I'm subconsciously concentrating my ears too much on keeping them from falling out of my ears, much like sunglasses from sliding down your nose, even though they are very secure most of the time. Know what I mean?,I also haven't thoroughly tested the mic quality during phone calls, but I can say I haven't had anyone notice an issue yet. Look to other reviews for more on that, battery life, and bluetooth connectivity distance.,CON: While the outer fabric of the charging/storage case gives it a premium look, I'd rather have a smoother surface so that I can slip it in or out of my pocket easier. Also, the tiny white LED dot indicator isn't very informative or useful for battery level or case-charging percentage/completion. Not really sure what the designers had in mind with that dot, but I wish it had an actual number percentage window, or, at the very least, a single color-changing LED that shows green, yellow, or red for charging completion or battery life left.,Overall, these bluetooth earbuds come highly recommended from a self-proclaimed audio snob :-)
